The main takeaway from our work is that

diffusion within adsorbing films is important for solute transport at very low water contents, and that the effective diffusion coefficient can be predicted from the bulk diffusion coefficient and the impedance factor, which is determined by the water content and the surface tortuosity.

diffusion of solutes within water films in unsaturated media is not controlled by film thickness alone, and the effective diffusion coefficient decreases as a function of decreasing water content due to the influence of tortuosity.

diffusion in unsaturated porous media at very low water contents is controlled by diffusion within water films, and the effective diffusion coefficients can be accurately predicted by accounting for the reduced cross-sectional area and tortuosity of the water films.
